**Sundhedsklynge Fyn** is a regional healthcare cluster in Denmark that operates as a local organizational sub-unit of [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src5]. It is one of the many healthcare clusters monitored by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) to evaluate, benchmark, and improve the clinical management of [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] across the country [^src1]. 

The cluster is significant for its compliance with national clinical quality standards. Notably, Sundhedsklynge Fyn successfully met the national benchmark for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 90.7% [^src1]. Its performance is rigorously tracked across a wide array of quality indicators over multiple years, including 1-year, 2-year, and 5-year anticoagulation treatment coverage [^src2], [^src3], as well as the frequency of annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOAC therapy [^src4]. 

Beyond treatment adherence, the cluster's patient outcomes are closely monitored for adverse events and long-term risks. Data from the RKKP reports track the incidence of ischemic stroke (apopleksi) [^src4], serious bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6], heart failure development [^src7], and overall mortality [^src11]. Geographically, Sundhedsklynge Fyn is mapped alongside other Danish healthcare clusters—such as [[sundhedsklynge-lillebaelt|Sundhedsklynge Lillebælt]], [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]], and [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]]—to visualize the regional incidence of stroke among atrial fibrillation patients [^src4]. This comprehensive, multi-year monitoring allows regional and local health authorities to identify variations in clinical practice, assess case-mix effects, and drive targeted quality improvements in cardiovascular care [^src8].
